replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I rarely experience math anxiety. My background in physics and hands-on problem-solving has built confidence. replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: In the past year, I used AI tools like Wolfram Alpha for quick calculations and explanations. It helped me verify solutions and understand steps without overwhelming me. I found it useful but prefer human guidance for deeper conceptual clarity.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, ensure the equation is in standard form (ax² + bx + c = 0). Then, calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If positive, two real solutions; if zero, one real solution; if negative, complex solutions. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. These x-values are critical points. Substitute back into f(x) to find the corresponding y-values. Verify if they are maxima or minima using the second derivative test.
